- Cutover switch (maintainer, 2026-10-16, recorded as comment 6221962821 on #1961; read it in full first): .agents/repos.json carries a cutover switch that is OFF in the committed file until #1967 flips it in the cutover window. While it is off, .agents/hooks/typed-issue-hook.mjs keeps today's behaviour exactly (typed-creation enforcement on ImpowerGames/impower, pass-through for other repositories, none of the public-repository refusals). The guard behaviour #1962 specifies applies only while the switch is on. The acceptance criteria that say a public-repository command is refused are met with the switch on; with it off the same commands pass as they do today.

- Other orchestrations (#1904 and #1940) run on this machine with writers on sibling branches; reviewer slots and the vitest reservation are shared. - If SendMessage to the coordinator's local_ id fails with no agent reachable, run ListAgents and send to the session titled exactly 'ORCH #1961: private internal tracker'; that is the same coordinator. Any subagent you launch (a filer, a helper) reports to the coordinator, not to you: record 'filer launched, report pending' in your notes and continue rather than waiting on it. Keep all private artifacts under the artifact parent this brief names, never under the coordinator's scratchpad.

Once round 3's accepted fixes are verified, again after every later round's, and whenever another decision needs the user, send the coordinator a checkpoint report, then end your turn: the completed round, its planned reviewers and their exits, every report and adjudication comment id, the last reviewed commit and the current head, which accepted findings share an underlying mechanism, whether corrections introduced new defects, whether a broader or simpler repair would be better, the concrete residual risk, and what another round would establish.

Treat a refusal as a correction to make now.
The coordinator answers with a checkpoint decision it publishes on the PR. Launch a further round only under its extension, with reviewRoundLimit and extendedReviewAuthorization exactly as that decision gives them. Never waive your own review or post a checkpoint decision: accepting unreviewed corrections is the coordinator's decision alone, and under it the PR stays draft until the coordinator acts.
Your review jobs keep their own ownership, round counts, freezes and process-exit checks, and the machine-wide reviewer and test reservations stay authoritative. The coordinator holds no lock on your worktree.
Never merge, and never mark the PR ready before the review gates pass.
Final report, as fields: model, effort, permissionMode, pr, reviewedHead, rounds, findings, verification, ci, next (your model, effort and permission mode as you read them yourself; the PR number; the last independently reviewed commit; rounds used per reviewer route; outstanding findings or None; the verification evidence; the state of each CI check on the final head; your next action), plus any changes after the reviewed commit.
